title: Shifted multiplicative characters

problem.name: Shifted multiplicative characters
problem.statement_latex: Let $\chi$ be a known nontrivial multiplicative character of $\mathbb F_q$, extended by $\chi(0)=0$. Given $f(x)=\chi(x+s)$ by coherent queries, recover the shift $s\in\mathbb F_q$. The Legendre character is the principal example.
problem.statement_text: Let $\chi$ be a known nontrivial multiplicative character of $\mathbb F_q$, extended by $\chi(0)=0$. Given $f(x)=\chi(x+s)$ by coherent queries, recover the shift $s\in\mathbb F_q$. The Legendre character is the principal example.

strength.description_latex: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.
strength.description_text: Exponential or subexponential to polynomial in the strongest stated regime.

evidence.description_latex: The quantum bound improves a published classical algorithm in the stated regime; the comparison is between algorithmic upper bounds.
evidence.description_text: The quantum bound improves a published classical algorithm in the stated regime; the comparison is between algorithmic upper bounds.

hardware.description_latex: The algorithm requires coherent input access and fault-tolerant execution of the stated procedure; its circuit and workspace requirements depend on that access implementation.

quantum.headline_latex: $\operatorname{poly}(\log q)$ gates and constantly many oracle calls by van Dam--Hallgren--Ip, using Fourier transforms and Gauss-sum phases.
quantum.headline_text: $\operatorname{poly}(\log q)$ gates and constantly many oracle calls by van Dam–Hallgren–Ip, using Fourier transforms and Gauss-sum phases.

classical.headline_latex: $\widetilde O(q)$ time by testing candidate shifts against $O(\log q)$ sampled evaluations; the query information can be collected with polynomially many calls. The difficulty is computational recovery from those evaluations.
